quote: Was den functionentheoretischen Theil des Problems betrifft: Ausdehnung{+ + +} des Kroneckerschen Theorems, dass alle Abelschen Körper Kreiskörper sind
english: As regards the function-theoretic part of the problem: extension of Kronecker's theorem that all Abelian fields are cyclotomic fields
topic: The page ends a note citing Lie's claim that every real transformation can be regarded as generated by an infinitesimal one, then proposes a method for the function-theoretic part of extending Kronecker's theorem that all Abelian fields are cyclotomic fields: first determine number fields of relative degree a power of 2 whose relative discriminant contains only prime factors dividing 2.

triage.modern_statement: Generalize the Kronecker–Weber theorem (every finite abelian extension of Q lies in a cyclotomic field, i.e. is generated by special values of exp(2πiz)) to an arbitrary number field K. In other words, describe all abelian extensions of K explicitly, ideally as fields generated by special values of transcendental (analytic) functions. This is the 'function-theoretic' part. The method Hilbert sketches here (first handle relative extensions whose degree is a power of 2 and that are ramified only above 2) looks like a reduction step for the arithmetic part of a Kronecker–Weber-type proof. This step is an inference from the page summary and is not supported by a source.
triage.answered_by: This is Hilbert's 12th problem (Paris 1900), also known as Kronecker's Jugendtraum. Hilbert himself published a complete proof of the Kronecker–Weber theorem over Q in 1896 ('Ein neuer Beweis des Kronecker'schen Fundamentalsatzes über Abel'sche Zahlkörper'). Takagi and Artin's class field theory later described abelian extensions abstractly but not explicitly. Explicit constructions are known only in special cases: complex multiplication for imaginary quadratic fields, and Dasgupta–Kakde (2021) for totally real fields using p-adic Brumer–Stark units. The general case remains open.

evidence.claim: Hilbert's twelfth problem is the extension of the Kronecker–Weber theorem on abelian extensions of Q to any base number field; the general case is open.
Dasgupta and Kakde built the maximal abelian extension of totally real fields using the Brumer–Stark conjecture.
Dasgupta–Kakde, 'Brumer–Stark Units and Hilbert's 12th Problem': an unconditional solution of Hilbert's 12th problem for totally real fields that involves p-adic integration.
Hilbert published the first complete proof of the Kronecker–Weber theorem in 1896 ('Ein neuer Beweis des Kronecker'schen Fundamentalsatzes über Abel'sche Zahlkörper').
Real quadratic fields remain an active case: there is work on Kronecker's Jugendtraum / Hilbert's 12th problem for real quadratic fields through real multiplication.
A history of Hilbert's 12th problem (Schappacher) tracing it back to the Kronecker–Weber theorem.

triage.why: The note's wording, 'extension of Kronecker's theorem that all Abelian fields are cyclotomic fields' together with its 'function-theoretic part', is exactly the content of Hilbert's 12th problem as he posed it in 1900. Over Q the question was settled, including by Hilbert's own 1896 proof. Over imaginary quadratic fields it is settled by complex multiplication, and over totally real fields by Dasgupta–Kakde (2021, p-adic version). It is still open for general number fields, for example via an archimedean/Stark-unit version, real multiplication, or fields that are neither totally real nor CM. It remains an active research area. The specific reduction to 2-power extensions ramified only at 2 cannot be tied to a particular publication; it is probably a step toward Hilbert's 1896 work, but that is not confirmed by sources.
